segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Forty-Four. Apply to a given segment, in a given angle, a parallelogram equal in area to a given triangle. Let A B be the given segment, C the given triangle, and D the given angle. We apply to segment A B, in an angle equal to D, a parallelogram equal in area to triangle C.

subsegments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Forty-Four. Apply to a given segment, in a given angle, a parallelogram equal in area to a given triangle. segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: By Proposition Forty-Two, construct parallelogram B E F G equal in area to triangle C in angle E B G equal to angle D, placed so that B E is in a line with A B. Extend F G to H, draw A H through A parallel to B G, and construct segment H B. Because transversal H F falls on parallels A H and E F, interior angles A H F and H F E equal two right angles. Thus angles B H G and G F E are less than two right angles, so by the Fifth Postulate, H B and F E extended will meet. Extend them to meet at K, draw K L through K parallel to E A, and extend H A and G B to points L and M.

subsegments.text: By Proposition Forty-Two, construct parallelogram B E F G equal in area to triangle C in angle E B G equal to angle D, placed so that B E is in a line with A B. Extend F G to H, draw A H through A parallel to B G, and construct segment H B. Because transversal H F falls on parallels A H and E F, interior angles A H F and H F E equal two right angles. Thus angles B H G and G F E are less than two right angles, so by the Fifth Postulate, H B and F E extended will meet. Extend them to meet at K, draw K L through K parallel to E A, and extend H A and G B to points L and M.

segments.text: Now H L K F is a parallelogram with diameter H K, having parallelograms H A B G and B M K E about H K, and complements A B M L and B E F G. By Proposition Forty-Three, complement A B M L equals complement B E F G, which was constructed equal to triangle C; therefore A B M L equals triangle C. Moreover, by Proposition Fifteen, vertical angle A B M equals angle E B G, which equals angle D; so angle A B M equals angle D. Therefore parallelogram A B M L, equal to triangle C, has been applied to segment A B in angle A B M equal to angle D, as was required to do.
